prompt: What really caused the 2008 financial crisis? Tell it as a story starting from the US housing boom, include subprime mortgages, securitization, Lehman Brothers and the government response.

plan.title: What Really Caused the 2008 Financial Crisis
plan.description: The 2008 financial crisis grew from a US housing boom, subprime mortgages and securitization. It climaxed with Lehman Brothers' bankruptcy and a massive government response.

beats.narration: Banks handed mortgages to almost anyone. Housing prices soared, and risky subprime loans were bundled into securities that rating agencies called safe.
Then prices fell. Borrowers stopped paying, those securities collapsed, and in September 2008 Lehman Brothers went bankrupt.
Panic spread worldwide. Washington stepped in with the bailout program TARP to steady the banks.
One lesson: when everyone treats risk as safe, one fall can shake the world.

props.text: Hidden risk can shake the whole world.

warnings: length: the narration totals 68 words in 4 beats but a 30-second video needs about 58 (between 52 and 58). Cut about 10 words: 3 to 4 beats of about 19 words each (you averaged 17; count the words of every beat), one idea, no preamble and no recap; keep the hook and the last line
